What degraded

  • tests/article_edition.mjs could not import Playwright as an ES module in this checkout, as on November 12th, and is left to CI. The article was inspected at desktop and phone width with a CommonJS Playwright script instead.
  • The Grid Watch series is still missing November 1st and ERCOT can't backfill it. The collector is cron's and nothing here was changed.
  • No dossier declares a verbatim block, so no on-frame string was held to a quote (verbatim_check WARN).

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it All 245 Large Loads answered ERCOT, and cooling questions had the highest N/A rate, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Every Large Load answered ERCOT.

That is all 245 loads of 75 MW or greater. The count comes from a preliminary ERCOT summary for the utility commission's November 5th open meeting. In total 433 of 465 loads responded, covering about 177 GW. West Texas holds 41% of the capacity requested, 73 GW.

What went unanswered?

Respondents answered 83% of nearly 67,000 questions. Cooling questions drew N/A answers at the highest rate. Respondents indicated many projects had not determined their final cooling configuration. Projects asking to energize in 2028 or later answered N/A 30% more often than those due sooner.

ERCOT is targeting a published final report on December 10th.

Will the December 10th report count how many projects still haven't settled on cooling?

#ERCOT #PUCT #WestTexas

The drawing scales are computed in compute.py, and so is cooling's rank by N/A rate, from the summary's own tables. One copper bar stands for one GW, 177 from c4 and each zone's figure from c11 to c14. One reel stands for each of the 245 Large Loads in c7. The trench is grated for 83% of its drawn length, from c17. On the close-up pad the longer row of capped stubs is the shorter row grown by the 2028 figure in c20.

The machine changed itself

  • deck_chassis refuses a chassis model whose stated origin K.make would re-centre
    A model whose comment puts its origin at an end, corner, back or wall point, and which doesn't keep that origin, is now refused for decks after today. K.make re-centres such a model silently, which is how no. 76's cable trench landed off its planned ends on three frames (queue repeat 2). No shipped deck changes result, and the self-test runs 33 cases, three of which fail with the rule switched off.
  • No kit lift in this weekly pass
    Lifting no. 76's own chassis models would have re-rendered a deck still under scoring, and the kit person's fix was deferred for the second pass running for the same reason.
  • Three proposals left for a maintainer
    In UPGRADE_BACKLOG under 2026-11-13: K.make recording the offset it applies plus a wall anchor (txkit.js is human lane), a GATE_LESSONS entry, and a rule for when a weekly pass may change a kit default.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record first. Re-verify read 268 urls behind 1,155 claims and stamped 116 items checked and unchanged. Three items moved: the screwworm count on tx-2026-0218 rose to 72 Texas premises in 24 counties, Pflugerville's Proposition B passed in unofficial returns on tx-2026-0075, and tx-2026-0072 gained ERCOT's November 5th papers. Nothing was admitted, because both new events belonged to items the record already held. The deck. ERCOT issued its data center impact questionnaire to 465 loads and 433 answered, covering about 177 GW. Every one of the 245 Large Loads responded. West Texas holds 41 percent of the capacity requested, 73 GW. Respondents answered 83 percent of nearly 67,000 questions, and cooling drew N/A answers at the highest rate of any category. A final report is targeted for December 10th. Two hard fails, both found by the panel and both repaired. Round 1: the cover, frame 6, the caption and the title all said cooling was the largest share of unanswered questions. ERCOT's own page 5 table puts cooling at about 1,540 of 11,554 N/A answers, fourth of five, and first only by rate. ERCOT's own sentence is ambiguous and its chart shows it means the rate. Every surface, the record's claim on tx-2026-0072 and the web edition now say cooling drew N/A answers at the highest rate, and compute.py derives both ranks from the tables rather than taking either on trust. Frame 6's art was rebuilt twice and then simplified to four empty pads, because a trench for the unanswered share standing beside four pads the hook named as cooling read as cooling being larger than the whole. Round 2: the first comment still described that trench after the frame had dropped it, and the sentence was replaced with one describing only what the frames draw. The deck shipped at the round cap with a panel median of 6.928, under round 1's 8.0 bar by 1.072 and round 2's 7.7 rung by 0.772. No hard fail survived into round 3. The artwork median, 6.5, is under the 8.5 craft floor, which stands down at the cap. All three round 3 judges named the same four frames weakest: the trench relief reading as a floor vent, the copper pack reading as a timber crate, the four zone packs reading as a bar chart, and the plan table frame too small in its bay. The copper was rebuilt through four materials across three frames and still read as wood, so that is the engine's defect rather than this deck's, and it is queued. Left undone past the cap, named by every judge: the deck never says why an undecided cooling design should reach a Texan. The water board's own questions rode inside this questionnaire (c36) and the commission's December 17th open meeting (c38) were both verified and both went unused. The next run on this story should lead with them. Did the run wait on a human. prompt_audit measured 1,820 tool calls and flagged 49 with a permission decision between 1.0 and 21.3 seconds, nearly all of them Agent spawns, every one of them released with nobody answering. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:03:23 UTC, judged the session unattended at session start with the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED reading 0, and refused nothing. Nothing in this run stopped for a person.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
